title: ContributorCredit model + credit-vs-deidentify policy (stable pseudonymous ids, opt-in named credit, DUA-governed)
context: PLAN v0.2 resolves a design contradiction between volunteer attribution and privacy-by-default PII removal: the ContributorCredit model emits a stable pseudonymous non-reversible contributor id so a volunteer's records stay linkable for credit and consensus without exposing identity. A volunteer's real name is emitted only under an explicit opt-in (opt-in-named); otherwise credit is pseudonymous or an aggregate acknowledgment. The partner's DUA governs the credit policy per dataset and the default-on-ambiguity is the more protective option. This is a new M2 exit criterion not covered by any existing task. Depends on csp-privacy-009 and csp-policy-003.
objective: Implement the ContributorCredit model (salted non-reversible pseudonymous contributor id; opt-in-named / pseudonymous / aggregate-acknowledgment credit policy configurable per dataset, DUA-governed) in @csp/privacy, and document the credit-vs-deidentify policy so the License+PII reviewer can confirm no identity leak occurs via the credit field.
acceptanceCriteria: ContributorCredit model implemented: salted non-reversible pseudonymous contributor id emitted by default; recordedBy-style field carries the pseudonym, not the observer's real identity
Credit policy enum (opt-in-named | pseudonymous | aggregate-acknowledgment) configurable per dataset in the pipeline spec; default is pseudonymous
Real name emitted only under opt-in-named with explicit opt-in recorded in the dataset policy; aggregate-acknowledgment emits no per-record credit field
Test asserts that a pseudonymous run produces no real-name output even when source data contains observer names
Credit-vs-deidentify policy documented in docs/policy/ and referenced from the license/PII/sensitivity gate checklist (csp-policy-003 output)
output: A PR adding ContributorCredit to @csp/privacy, the credit-policy configuration, CI tests, and the credit-vs-deidentify policy document.
